We Do Consulting Differently

Berkeley Research Group (BRG) is a global consulting firm that helps its clients, which consist of leading organizations and businesses, advance in three key areas: disputes and investigations, corporate finance, and performance improvement and advisory. We are an integrated group of experts, industry leaders, academics, data scientists, and economists, working beyond borders and disciplines. We harness our collective expertise to deliver the inspired insights and practical strategies our clients need to stay ahead of what’s next.

About the Role

The work of an intern can have quantitative and qualitative aspects, depending on the needs of specific projects and the intern’s skills and interests. Projects range from subject matter research to data collection, to the preparation of economic, statistical, financial, and other forms of analysis. You will build technical skills and contribute to work that shapes important legal and business outcomes.

The intern program will start Fall 2026 with a planned end of May 2027. Interns will work up to 20 hours per week mainly in our downtown office. We’re committed to helping our interns succeed by providing them with dedicated mentors, training programs, hands-on learning opportunities and support from industry experts. Our internship program is a pipeline program, and we aim to convert interns to full-time Associates after graduation, assuming the role is a fit on both ends.

What You’ll Do

- Develop a practical understanding of industries, markets, legal claims, and business issues relevant to each engagement by gathering and reviewing information from our clients and their business, academic literature, legal documents, specialized industry resources, commercial databases, or other sources appropriate for the unique requirements of a project.

- Identify, collect, develop, maintain, analyze and review data, qualitative materials, spreadsheets and other files as dictated by complex project needs.

- Combine programming, model building, and statistical analysis skills using relational database and statistical programs to analyze a variety of subjects with software such as SQL, R, Stata, SAS, Python, or Snowflake.

- Interact with senior staff, experts, and clients to clearly communicate questions, findings, economic and business concepts, and recommendations.

- Demonstrate creativity and efficient analytical skills to develop novel solutions tailored to unique projects.

- Provide valuable contributions to client deliverables and expert reports.

Qualifications

- Progression towards a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Economics, Mathematics, Data Science, Statistics, Accounting, Business, Finance, Healthcare Administration or a related analytical field, with an expected graduation date between Winter 2027 and Summer 2028.

- 3.6 GPA or higher preferred.

- Demonstrated interest in applying analytics to business, financial, legal, regulatory, or policy questions.

- Strong quantitative, research, problem-solving, and written communication skills.

- Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, client-service environment.

- Attention to detail, intellectual curiosity, and a commitment to producing high-quality work.

- Experience with statistical, econometric and programming tools such as Excel, Stata, R, Python, SQL or similar platforms is preferred.

- Fluency with AI tools is desirable.

- Candidates must be able to submit verification of their legal right to work in the United States, without company sponsorship now or in the future.

Our Practice Areas

This internship opportunity is specifically within our Health Analytics Practice. We tackle complex legal and operational challenges in the healthcare industry using data-driven, objective, and innovative approaches. Our experts lead advisory, risk management, and litigation matters, combining deep healthcare industry expertise with cutting edge research, analytics and financial modeling.

Locations

This internship position is in the Chicago office. Interns are expected to work in the office as much as possible to take full advantage of the mentorship, collaboration, and relationship-building opportunities that support their professional growth.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should submit a copy of their resume, cover letter and transcript through the job posting. You can find the job application deadlines listed below:

- Deadline for priority review: September 5

- Deadline for secondary review: September 19

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. A member of the recruiting team will be in touch if there is an interest in scheduling interviews.

Salary Range: $25/hour - $40/hour

Consulting Magazine recognized BRG as a Best Firms to Work for in 2025.

BRG combines world-leading academic credentials with world-tested business expertise and purpose-built emerging technologies. Our culture centers on agility and connectivity which sets us apart and gets you ahead.

We're looking for an Salesforce Developer Intern to help build, configure, and maintain solutions on the Salesforce platform. You'll work alongside senior developers and business analysts to implement customizations, automate business processes, and support integrations across Sales, Marketing, and Operations. This is a great opportunity for someone early in their career who wants to grow their development skills within a widely-used enterprise platform.

Development & Configuration

- Build and maintain custom objects, fields, page layouts, and record types in Salesforce
- Write Apex classes, triggers, and Lightning Web Components (LWC) under guidance from senior developers
- Configure Flows, Process Builder, and validation rules to automate business processes
- Support declarative (clicks-not-code) solutions before recommending custom code

Testing & Quality

- Write unit tests for Apex code to meet code coverage and quality standards
- Debug and troubleshoot issues in existing customizations and integrations
- Support user acceptance testing (UAT) and validate fixes before deployment
- Follow release management and deployment best practices (sandboxes, change sets, CI/CD tools)

Integrations & Data

- Assist with integrations between Salesforce and other business systems (marketing automation, ERP, support tools)
- Support data migration, imports, and data quality efforts using tools like Data Loader
- Help maintain APIs and middleware connections (e.g., REST/SOAP callouts, MuleSoft, or similar)

Collaboration & Support

- Partner with business analysts and stakeholders in Sales, Marketing, and Operations to understand requirements
- Translate business requirements into technical solutions within the Salesforce platform
- Document technical designs, configurations, and code changes
- Provide day-to-day support for Salesforce users, resolving tickets and bugs as needed

AI & Automation Development

- Help build and configure an interactive AI support agent within Salesforce (e.g., Agentforce/Einstein or custom LWC integration with an LLM API) to automate responses to common user questions
- Develop Apex classes and Lightning Web Components to connect the AI agent to Salesforce data (cases, knowledge articles, CRM records)
- Configure and train the AI agent using knowledge base content, FAQs, and support workflows
- Write test cases to validate AI agent responses, accuracy, and proper escalation to human agents
- Monitor and iterate on AI agent performance, expanding automated coverage over time

Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field (or equivalent experience)
- 0–2 years of experience developing on the Salesforce platform (internships, coursework, or personal projects count)
- Basic understanding of Apex, Visualforce, and/or Lightning Web Components
- Familiarity with object-oriented programming concepts
- Understanding of relational databases and basic SQL/SOQL
- Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail
- Willingness to learn Salesforce best practices and platform updates

Preferred (Not Required)

- Salesforce Platform Developer I certification (or in progress)
- Salesforce Administrator certification
- Experience with version control (e.g., Git) and CI/CD tools
- Exposure to HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
- Interest in or exposure to AI/LLM tools (e.g., Salesforce Einstein/Agentforce, OpenAI/Anthropic APIs, chatbot frameworks)
- Coursework, internship, or project experience involving CRM or business systems

What Success Looks Like

- You deliver clean, well-tested code that meets business requirements
- You become comfortable navigating the Salesforce ecosystem (Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, and related tools)
- You build strong working relationships with business analysts and stakeholders across the company
- You progress toward a Salesforce Platform Developer II certification and a mid-level developer role

- Create practical solutions to problems presented in the trading environment on either a systematic equity trading desk or a fixed income options desk

- Conduct statistical analysis of market data, historical trends, and relationships across multiple asset classes

- Formulate and apply mathematical modeling, quantitative methods and machine learning techniques to identify and capture trading opportunities

- Work closely with traders and researchers to build and refine research infrastructure and tools

- Proficient programming skills with experience exploring large datasets

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills including a solid foundation of statistics knowledge

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills to report research results as well as methodologies

You’ll complete an options course taught by an experienced trader and participate in a technology immersion course to better understand how technology and trading intersect.

What You'll Do

You’ll work directly with the AI team, taking responsibility for well-scoped pieces of real systems, with mentorship from senior engineers.

Benchmarks & Evaluation

- Contribute to APIFlow-Bench, our open-source benchmark for real API-development work: design and review benchmark tasks and their mock API environments, extend the evaluation harness and task-generation pipeline in Python, and help maintain the public multi-model leaderboard with statistical confidence intervals.

- Help build a new action-level AI safety benchmark: instead of grading what a model says, it scores what an agent actually does inside a simulated enterprise API environment. You’ll work on scenario design, threat modeling (prompt injection, data exfiltration, permission overreach), and auditable evaluation design.

Model Training & Efficiency

- Fine-tune open-weight models for tool calling and agentic tasks (SFT, distillation, and RL) using PyTorch and the open-source training ecosystem, on both managed training platforms and self-managed cloud GPUs.

- Design and run experiments with rigor: evaluate every training run on our benchmarks, support ablation studies and error analysis, track experiments, and report results honestly, including cost.

- Evaluate ultra-low-bit quantized models for on-device use: extend our quantized vs. full-precision benchmark comparisons and analyze where and why they diverge.

Agent Systems & Engineering Practice

- Help build the next generation of Postman’s in-product AI agent (Agent Mode): a deliberately minimal agent architecture that calls LLM APIs directly (tool loops, multi-step execution, checkpointing), primarily in TypeScript. No prior TypeScript is required; strong Python fundamentals transfer quickly.

- Read the source code of open-source agent harnesses and turn what you learn into design specs and prototypes.

- Document experiments, design decisions, and runbooks so your work is legible to the next person; flag safety, fairness, or privacy concerns you observe in model or agent behavior.

- Experience fine-tuning open-weight LLMs (SFT, LoRA, RL, or distillation), with the improvement measured on a benchmark.
